Rarity.maps_to: Potion.rarity = 'rare' (potions.py:968), read by shop.MerchantPotionEntry pricing and by potion_pools.POTION_POOL's rarity bucket (potion_pools.py:38-65)
Rarity.rationale: EXECUTED, not asserted: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-attrs` extracts PotionRarity from every C# model and diffs it against the sim class attribute over all 51 units and reports 0 mismatches. Rarity is observable in the sim (it sets the shop price and the reward-roll bucket), so this is a behavioural verdict rather than a field copy.

Usage.maps_to: no explicit attribute; the sim's only potion-use entry point is CombatState.use_potion (combat.py:583-616), which cannot be reached outside a combat
Usage.rationale: PotionUsage.CombatOnly means the game's Use button is live only during a fight. The sim reaches that by construction: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-usage` finds exactly one `def use_potion` in sts2_rl/, on CombatState, and the conformance driver only dispatches the recording's UsePotion command inside a live fight (conformance/combat_driver.py:16,263-289). The absence of a `usage` attribute is therefore not a dropped guard for this unit -- but it IS a real gap for the four AnyTime potions, which is where the divergence is filed (blood_potion, entropic_brew, foul_potion, fruit_juice).

TargetType.maps_to: no attribute -- `targeted` stays False, so CombatState.use_potion passes target=None (combat.py:608) and the potion applies to ctx.player (potions.py:971-987)
TargetType.rationale: TargetType.Self in a single-player run always resolves to the owner: PotionModel.EnqueueManualUse defaults `target` to `Owner.Creature` when it is a valid target (PotionModel.cs:240-243) and IsValidTarget's Self/AnyPlayer arms accept exactly that creature (PotionModel.cs:280-287). The multiplayer half -- AnyPlayer letting you throw the potion at an ally, and CanThrowAtAlly (PotionModel.cs:381-388) gating it on `RunState.Players.Count > 1` -- is out of scope by the shared contract and noted in maps_to rather than verdicted as a divergence.

CanonicalVars (protected override, Disti.rationale: `new RepeatVar(3)`, read as `Repeat.IntValue` at DistilledChaos.cs:27. No ascension branch.

OnUse (protected override, DistilledChao.rationale: The whole content of this port is the TWO-PHASE shape of CardPileCmd.AutoPlayFromDrawPile (CardPileCmd.cs:931-966) and the sim reproduces it. Phase 1 pulls `count` cards one at a time, calling ShuffleIfNecessary BEFORE each pull and moving each pulled card straight to PileType.Play so the next pull cannot see it (CardPileCmd.cs:939-955); potions.py:974-983 loops the same way, reshuffling only when the draw pile is empty (the ShuffleIfNecessary condition) and popping each card out of the pile as it goes. Phase 2 then plays the collected cards in pull order (CardPileCmd.cs:956-965 vs potions.py:984-987). Both `break` when a pull comes back empty. See the guards for position, the death check and forceExhaust.

guards.what: N1: CardPilePosition.Top -- C# takes `drawPile.Cards.FirstOrDefault()` and the sim takes `draw_pile.pop()`
guards.rationale: Opposite ends of the list, same card, because the two codebases hold the draw pile in opposite orientations. player.py:290 states the sim's convention inline -- `card = self.draw_pile.pop()  # end of list = top of pile` -- and it is the same convention the ordinary draw uses, so 'the top card' means the same card that a Draw would have taken. Checked rather than assumed because Top/Bottom is exactly the kind of orientation flip PROMPT.md bug class 8 is about, and getting it wrong here would silently play the three WRONG cards while leaving every count identical.

guards.what: N2: phase 2's per-card guard -- C# breaks on `item.Owner.Creature.IsDead` only; the sim also breaks on `ctx.combat.is_over`
guards.rationale: SETTLED ON THE MERITS: the sim's extra clause is not an extra rule, it is the same rule read one level up. C#'s loop breaks only on player death (CardPileCmd.cs:958-964), but every iteration then calls CardCmd.AutoPlay, which itself opens `if (CombatManager.Instance.IsOverOrEnding || card.Owner.Creature.IsDead) return;` (CardCmd.cs:53-56) -- so a card pulled after the first auto-play won the fight is a no-op in C# too. The sim's CombatState.auto_play_card carries the same guard (combat.py:524-525) AND the potion checks it, which is belt-and-braces rather than a divergence: in both codebases the cards after the winning play do nothing and stay out of every pile. Verified against the C# rather than inferred from the loop, because 'the sim stops early where the game keeps going' would have been a real state divergence.

guards.what: N3: `forceExhaust: false` sets ExhaustOnNextPlay = false on each card (CardPileCmd.cs:960) and the sim sets nothing
guards.rationale: The assignment is `item.ExhaustOnNextPlay = forceExhaust`, i.e. an unconditional write of `false`, so the only way it could differ from the sim's no-op is if some other effect had set the flag true on one of these three cards and this potion CLEARED it. The sim has no per-card exhaust-on-next-play flag at all, so there is nothing to clear and nothing to preserve; the potions and cards that force an exhaust in the sim do it at the exhaust site instead. Recorded because a bare `= false` reads like dead code and is not always.

guards.what: N4: DistilledChaos is the only potion that AUTO-PLAYS, so it is the only one whose OnUse can nest another card's OnPlay
guards.rationale: Relevant because it is the concrete shape guard W4's dormancy argument turns on: this potion is the one live way for a potion frame to contain a card frame. It stays dormant because the missing depth counter only matters to Unceasing Top's empty-hand draw, and W4 names what would make it live. The auto-play verb's own semantics (unplayable cards moving to the result pile, ShouldPlay, CombatTargets targeting) belong to audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json.
